key_insight: A pretrained generative proposer can find more high-scoring quantum LDPC codes per expensive evaluation than tuned search baselines.
engineering_relevance: Learning from previous code evaluations can stretch limited search budgets when strong quantum error-correcting codes are rare.
method: Construct lifted-product codes one group element at a time with a GFlowNet.
Train on earlier search scores to sample codes in proportion to a power of their score, then freeze the model.
Rank batches of generated candidates before paying to evaluate selected codes.
evidence_signal: For distance-scored codes with 180 physical qubits, ranking 10 draws per paid evaluation found over twice as many new, training-inequivalent top-scoring codes as tuned parallel tempering and over 3.5 times as many as a supervised screen ranking 10 random candidates.
watch_item: The advantage depends on the comparison: the supervised screen won at batch size 100, and soft Q-learning matched or exceeded GFlowQEC across the two tested noise biases.
paper_title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
